sources.entry: linkding - Minimal bookmark management with a fast and clean UI. Simple installation through Docker and can run on your Raspberry Pi. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: linkding is a self-hosted bookmark manager with a minimal, fast UI that is designed to be installed easily with Docker.
summary.what_it_does: linkding is a bookmark manager intended to be hosted on your own server. It organizes bookmarks with tags and supports bulk editing, Markdown notes, and read-it-later functionality. It automatically fetches titles, descriptions and icons for bookmarked sites, and can archive websites either as local HTML files or on the Internet Archive. Bookmarks can be imported and exported in Netscape HTML format, and shared with other users or guests. Integration points named in the README include browser extensions for Firefox and Chrome, a bookmarklet, a REST API, SSO via OIDC or authentication proxies, and installation as a Progressive Web App.
use_cases: archive web pages locally or on Internet Archive
share bookmarks with teammates or guests
how_to_run: Install linkding on your own server using Docker (see the project documentation at linkding.link)
Create a user: uv run manage.py createsuperuser --username=joe --email=joe@example.com
notable: Browser extensions for Firefox and Chrome plus a bookmarklet
Automatic archiving to local HTML or Internet Archive
SSO via OIDC or authentication proxies
Can run on a Raspberry Pi according to the awesome-selfhosted listing
caveats: Development setup requires Python 3.13, uv and Node.js
The README says it is intended to be minimal, and it may decline PRs for features outside its goals
